2022_229_m121421bdmtg.paragraph: Approved minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held December 14, 2021 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:02 p.m. and adjourned at 8:13 p.m. In lieu of the Pledge of Allegiance the Board held a moment of silence for the students lost in the Oxford High School shooting, recognized the TSD Preschool inclusion program, and passed four resolutions. The largest was Resolution 21-090, awarding roof replacement bids totaling $1,432,597.95 to JD Candler and Royal West Roofing; the Board also awarded bid pack 33 for windows and doors at $696,983.00 and approved $162,922.95 in Nightlock lockdown hardware.
2022_229_m121421bdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held December 14, 2021 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. and the meeting adjourned at 8:13 p.m. Minutes signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (GH/jh).

**Attendance**
Present with Mr. Schmidt: Board members Anne, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, and Wilson. Mr. Gottlieb was absent. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, Keyser, Young, and West. Approximately 35 members of the audience attended. In lieu of the Pledge of Allegiance, Mr. Schmidt asked everyone to stand for a moment of silence and prayer honoring the students lost in the Oxford High School shooting.

**Recognition — TSD Preschool Inclusion**
The Board recognized the TSD Preschool inclusion program, in which students with special needs attend school with typically developing peers and special education and related services are integrated into all aspects of the program. Erin Keyser, Early Childhood Director, shared a video and introduced her team: Lauren DeGrazia, School Social Worker; Elizabeth Neuville, General Education Teacher; Katie Drinkard, Teacher Consultant; and Grace Lynch, Speech & Language Pathologist.

**Additions & Deletions**
Dr. Machesky removed agenda item 10.A, the Legislative Report from State Representative Kuppa, because Representative Kuppa was out of the country due to a family emergency. The District and Board planned to meet with Senator McMorrow and Representative Kuppa in January 2022.

**Resolution 21-089 — Consent Agenda**
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Dr. Wilson; approved items A through G: corrected minutes of the October 19, 2021 Board meeting; minutes of the November 9, 2021 Board Workshop; minutes of the November 16, 2021 Board meeting; Sex Education Advisory Board for 2021-2023; Treasurer's Report for October 2021; Budget Amendment #1; and Hill Coil & Condensing Unit Replacement. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

**Resolution 21-090 — Roofing Replacement Program**
Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mrs. Hammond; expenditure from the Capital Projects Fund and Building Site & Sinking Funds.

| Contractor | Scope | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JD Candler | Athens High School, Schroeder | $740,910.00 |
| Royal West Roofing | Troy High School | $623,469.00 |
| Contingency (5%) | | $68,218.95 |
| **TOTAL** | | **$1,432,597.95** |

Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

**Resolution 21-091 — Construction, Windows & Doors (Barnard, Bemis & IAE)**
Moved by Dr. Wilson, supported by Mr. Hauff; bid pack 33 awarded as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund.

| Vendor | Scope | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Environmental Glass Inc. | Exterior Doors | $567,000.00 |
| Triangle Window Fashions, Inc. | Roller Shades | 13,540.00 |
| Environmental Glass Inc. | Strategic Change Order | 70,000.00 |
| Contingency (8%) | | 46,443.00 |
| **TOTAL RECOMMENDED AWARD** | | **$696,983.00** |

Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

**Resolution 21-092 — Door Lock Hardware**
Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Mrs. Anne; purchase of Nightlock Lockdown hardware in the amount of $162,922.95 from Taylor Brothers Door Lock, LLC, approved as an expenditure of the General Fund, 2019 Capital Projects Bond and/or the Building Site & Sinking Fund. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

**Student Representatives**
Alyssa McLarty (Troy College and Career High School), Yara Mashal (International Academy-East), Sarayu Bethamcherla (Troy High School), and Sasha Palmkoeck (Athens High School) reported on events and activities at their schools.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda)**
Six speakers addressed the Board: Dr. Dick Young on a proposed school safety review committee; Sarah Krieger and Mrs. Katie MacFarland on high school library books and the book selection process; Mrs. Kacy Bailey on quarantine procedures and iPad parental controls; Mr. Ollie Apahidean on school media center content; and Mr. Joe Thilman in support of the District's mask mandate.

**Announcements**
Mr. Schmidt announced the next Board Workshop for Tuesday, January 4 at 6:00 p.m. and the next Organizational and regular Board Meeting for Tuesday, January 18 at 7:00 p.m., both at the Services Building.
2022_229_m121421bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held Tuesday, December 14, 2021 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Anne, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, and Wilson. Mr. Gottlieb was absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, Keyser, Young, and West. There were approximately 35 members of the audience. The minutes carry the notation GH/jh and are signed "Respectfully submitted, Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education."

Opening. Mr. Schmidt suggested that in lieu of the Pledge of Allegiance, everyone stand to honor the students lost in the Oxford High School shooting and share in a moment of silence and prayer for all of those affected by the tragedy.

Recognition — TSD Mission Moment: TSD Preschool Inclusion. The Board recognized the TSD Preschool for its inclusion program. The minutes describe inclusive education as a system in which students with special needs attend school with typically developing peers, and an inclusive preschool system as one that integrates special education and related services into all aspects of its program, making it possible to address the needs of all children. In Troy this means collaboration among all stakeholders, including both general education and special education staff as well as families and administration. The minutes note that the Troy School community has invested in ongoing shared learning to ensure best practices are implemented and staff is being responsive to students, and that equity and inclusion remain a priority, with the TSD Preschool committed to ensuring a learning environment where every student feels a sense of belonging. Erin Keyser, Early Childhood Director, was invited to share a video demonstrating examples of the inclusion program and then introduced her team: Lauren DeGrazia, School Social Worker; Elizabeth Neuville, General Education Teacher; Katie Drinkard, Teacher Consultant; and Grace Lynch, Speech & Language Pathologist.

Additions and Deletions. Dr. Machesky indicated that agenda item 10.A, Legislative Report from State Representative Kuppa, needed to be deleted from the agenda because Representative Kuppa was out of the country due to a family emergency. The District and Board planned to meet with Senator McMorrow and Representative Kuppa in January 2022 for a legislative update.

Public Communication (Agenda Items). None.

General — Consent Agenda, Resolution 21-089. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Dr. Wilson that the Troy Board of Education take action to approve items A, B, C, D, E, F, and G on the consent agenda. Those items were: corrected minutes of the October 19, 2021 Board of Education meeting; minutes of the November 9, 2021 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the November 16, 2021 Board of Education meeting; Sex Education Advisory Board for 2021-2023; Treasurer's Report — October 2021; Budget Amendment #1; and Hill Coil & Condensing Unit Replacement. The vote was Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

Personnel. None. Curriculum. None.

Business — Roofing Replacement Program, Resolution 21-090. It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Hammond that the bid for roof replacement be awarded as follows and that the amount be approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund and Building Site & Sinking Funds. JD Candler was awarded Athens High School and Schroeder for $740,910.00. Royal West Roofing was awarded Troy High School for $623,469.00. A contingency of 5% was set at $68,218.95. The total stated was $1,432,597.95. The vote was Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

Business — Construction, Windows & Doors (Barnard, Bemis & IAE), Resolution 21-091. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mr. Hauff that the bid for bid pack 33 be awarded as follows and that this be approved as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund. Environmental Glass Inc. was awarded Exterior Doors at $567,000.00. Triangle Window Fashions, Inc. was awarded Roller Shades at 13,540.00. Environmental Glass Inc. was awarded a Strategic Change Order at 70,000.00. Contingency at 8% was 46,443.00. The total recommended award stated was $696,983.00. The vote was Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

Business — Door Lock Hardware, Resolution 21-092. It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne that the district purchase Nightlock Lockdown hardware in the amount of $162,922.95 from Taylor Brothers Door Lock, LLC, and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the General Fund, the 2019 Capital Projects Bond and/or the Building Site & Sinking Fund. The vote was Yes 6, No 0, Absent Gottlieb.

Reports from Student Representatives to the Board. Alyssa McLarty, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, shared a report on the events and activities happening in her school. Yara Mashal, student representative for International Academy-East, shared a report on the events and activities at her school. Sarayu Bethamcherla, student representative for Troy High School, shared a report on events and activities at her school. Sasha Palmkoeck, student representative for Athens High School, shared a report on events and activities at her school.

Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items). President Schmidt shared a statement providing the structure of how the evening's public participation would be conducted in compliance with the Open Meetings Act and reviewed the guidelines to be followed for public comment. Dr. Dick Young, a Troy resident for 37 years, addressed the Board about his proposal for a school safety review committee made up of sub-committees to keep students safe. Sarah Krieger, a TSD parent of three students, addressed the Board about a book in the high school library and read excerpts from pages in the book. Mrs. Katie MacFarland, a TSD parent, addressed the Board about flaws in the process of selecting books for the school library and read an excerpt from one of the books. Mrs. Kacy Bailey, a TSD parent of two students, addressed the Board about procedures for student quarantines and about her child's iPad and issues with parental controls not working appropriately. Mr. Ollie Apahidean, a TSD parent, addressed the Board about the media content in school media centers and read an excerpt from a book found in the high school library. Mr. Joe Thilman, a Troy resident, addressed the Board about his support of the mask mandate in the District.

Other — Legislative Update from State Representative Kuppa. This item was deleted from the agenda; State Representative Kuppa was out of the country due to a family emergency.

Board Member Comments. Dr. Philippart wished everyone a happy holiday, acknowledged the difficult last few months, and thanked Kerry Birmingham for the continued district communication. Mrs. Hammond echoed Dr. Philippart's sentiments and wished everyone happy holidays. Mrs. Anne shared the same sentiments and thanked the administration, teachers, students, and parents for their patience throughout the challenging times, wishing everyone happy holidays. Mr. Hauff shared a message of hope during the holiday season, asking people to pause, reflect, pray, and extend a hand to all, and wished everyone a Merry Christmas. Dr. Wilson echoed her colleagues and shared how much she appreciates the administrators for their leadership in the challenge of balancing both the tragedy and joy of the season.

Dr. Machesky thanked all employee groups for what they do for students every day. He indicated that it had been a challenging couple of years but that he believes in the community and that it will come through stronger. He also mentioned that Kerry Birmingham had sent out a survey to the district and community for suggestions on how the district should consider spending ESSER funds moving forward.

Mr. Schmidt thanked the TSD cabinet team for its resiliency and how quickly it steps up when there is a crisis. He mentioned that the internal crisis committee met within days of the shooting to make changes where necessary. He talked about the recent shooting and said he appreciates the support the District has provided to staff and students. He shared that he had talked with several students about their feelings and how safe they feel at school after the tragedy and was happy to hear that they felt supported and safe. He announced that the next Board Workshop would be held on Tuesday, January 4 at 6:00 p.m. at the Services Building and that the next Organizational and regular Board Meeting would be Tuesday, January 18 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building.

Adjournment. The meeting adjourned at 8:13 p.m.
